newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China LPG importers reeling under high Asia prices.
newsitem.headline: China LPG importers reeling under high Asia prices.

text.p: China's liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) importers are reeling under high Asian prices as strong winter demand coincides with more supplies from Middle East being diverted to the West, industry sources said on Monday.
Currently, LPG cargoes delivered to southern China cost $280-285 per tonne, higher than last winter when they cost $220-$225, the sources said.
They attributed the rapid rise in prices to the usual strong winter demand and unusually limited supplies in Asia especially after September.
Last October, the contract price (CP) for LPG sales averaged $162 per tonne for cargoes loading from Saudi Arabia. The contract price is the Middle East benchmark price for the sale of LPG.
But this October prices rose by $43 to $205 per tonne, the sources said.
Traders said they expected prices to continue to climb for the rest of the year as winter demand sets in.
They said, while the CP is unlikely to top $230-$233 by the end of this year, the highest since the benchmark price was introduced in 1994, it might do so by the first quarter of 1997.
A trader in Hong Kong told Reuters that Chinese refiners have also been asked to boost LPG output ahead of winter while buyers are discouraged from buying at current high prices.
"We will cut back on imports if prices continue to rise," said a Chinese trader in Zhuhai, southern China.
"Due to the escalating prices, we have already reduced our September imports by close to 20 percent, down from imports in August," a Chinese LPG importer in Shanghai told Reuters.
Industry sources said supplies were limited because Saudi Arabian LPG cargoes continued to be diverted to Europe, the United States and Latin America where prices are stronger.

They said since September, any excess supplies from Saudi Arabia have been absorbed by Mexico, after an explosion in July at the biggest gas processing plant run by state-owned Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex).
In August, Saudi ARAMCO sealed a term contract to supply Pemex between 240,000 and 250,000 tonnes of LPG for delivery between September and March.
Some industry sources also attributed the rapid rise in prices to the current high crude prices.
They said prices in the U.S were driven up partly by firm sentiment amid the recent crude price spike and by strong winter LPG demand for heating purposes.
